Maybe using a queue system where each request goes through a queue, then gets processed by a processor. Queueing here would be about managing the flow of requests, maybe with FIFO or priority queues. Tail latency is the time a request takes to reach the tail, which could be due to processing time or queue delays.

Cache transfer is about how data is moved between the cache and main memory. Disaggregation here means separating the cache into different parts, so each part can handle different tasks. Role switching refers to when the system switches between different roles (like CPU or GPU) to handle different tasks. Batch completion is when multiple requests are processed in a batch, which can affect throughput.

GPU utilization is about how much GPU resources are being used, which affects both latency and throughput. Throughput tradeoffs involve balancing between processing speed and the number of requests handled, which can be a trade-off between higher throughput and increased latency.
